page.layout: One column of running text, with numbered sections (LXXII., LXXIII., LXXIV.) set on their own lines and italic scripture references closing each section. Page number and running head at the top. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: & ad decipiendos simplices quosque, quasi au-reis sensibus & eloquiis argenti fulgore splen-dentibus imperitorum obstringunt aciem, & à suis adiutoribus sublimatur. In 10.cap. Ieremia.

Simulachra dogmatum suorum atq; men-dacii, artifici corde componunt, & venerantur ea quae à se sciant esse simulata. Nec sufficit eis error proprius, nisi simplices quosque eorum adoratione deceperint. Qui quaestum putant esse pietatem, & devorant domos viduarum, abutentesque vulgi imperitia, ita arte Dialectica, quasi ascia & terebro, lima & runcina formant Deum suum, & cudunt malleo, atque inaurant sermonis rhetorici venustate: quorum Deus venter est, & gloria in confusione eorum. In 44.cap. Esaia.

Non dubium est, quin istiusmodi perditio-nis filii habeant plurimos filios quoscunq; de-cęperunt, & occidant in profundis vallibus, & in barathro impietatis subter imminentes pe-tras, quæ semper minantur ruinas : quæ pro di-versitate mendacii & varietate dogmatum per-versorum plures appellantur petrę. Nos autem unam habemus petram quæ semper sequitur populum Dei, de qua bibebat quondam populus Israel, quando familiaritate Domini frue-batur. In 57.cap. Esaiæ.
Prudentium virorum dicta non capiunt, sed

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout (e.g. "suorum", "simulata", "sublimatur"). The printed hyphens at line ends are kept ("au-reis", "splen-dentibus", "perditio-nis", "de-cęperunt", "pe-tras", "di-versitate", "per-versorum", "frue-batur"). The printed "Efaia"/"Efaiæ" in the references was read as "Esaia"/"Esaiæ"; the initial letter is slightly ambiguous at this scan resolution. Numbered sections LXXII.–LXXIV. were kept as paragraphs, not headings. The final line "sed" is the last full line; "se ad" is the catchword at the right below it.
